answer.part: How rule is determined, including ties, tokens and Vagabond
answer.ruling: A player rules a clearing with more warriors plus buildings than each other player. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules; Eyrie rule a tie for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Tokens and pawns do not count. Vagabond cannot rule or stop another from ruling.

answers.evidence: Actions > Shared movement, crafting and battle

answer.part: Normal move legality, repeated moves, and rivers
answer.ruling: Move any positive number of your warriors/pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing; you must rule origin, destination, or both, and recheck rule for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including multiple times in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect says otherwise.

answers.evidence: Actions > Shared movement, crafting and battle

answer.ruling: Defender may play matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush, discarding defender's card and causing no ambush hits. Otherwise defender deals two immediate hits and discards it; if no attacking warriors or pawn remain, battle ends. Before-roll and after-roll effects resolve around the roll; attacker orders effects when both sides have same-timing effects. Higher die is attacker's hits, lower defender's (equal dice equal); rolled hits capped by own warriors (Alliance defending reverses dice; Vagabond uses undamaged swords). Add extra hits and subtract ignored hits; defender with no warriors gives attacker one defenseless hit (Vagabond instead if no undamaged swords). Each hit removes an opposing piece; side taking hits chooses order, but all warriors before buildings/tokens. Both sides deal counted hits, without recalculating caps. Removing enemy building/token scores one VP each, including as defender and outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage.

answers.evidence: Actions > Shared movement, crafting and battle

answer.part: Crafting costs, reuse, missing supply items and duplicate effects
answer.ruling: For each bottom-left icon, Marquise/Eyrie/Alliance activate one workshop/roost/sympathy respectively in a clearing matching that icon; a piece's suit is its clearing's suit and each piece activates at most once per turn. Vagabond exhausts one face-up undamaged hammer per icon and its current clearing must match every icon; the pawn can be reused repeatedly, but the hammer cost remains per icon. An item card cannot be crafted if its corresponding token is absent from map supply. Only an identical persistent effect already in your own play area prevents crafting it again; other players' copies do not.

answers.evidence: Actions > Shared movement, crafting and battle

answer.part: Dominance activation, VP threshold, win conditions, and activated card disposal
answer.ruling: During your Daylight at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area, remove your score marker, and stop scoring VP. At the start of your Birdsong, win by ruling three clearings of the matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit, or for bird dominance by ruling two diagonally opposite corner clearings. An activated card cannot be removed or replaced; meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately.

answer.part: Disposition of a dominance card spent for suit and taking one from availability
answer.ruling: A dominance card that would enter discard instead goes near the map as available. During your Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so the payment must be a bird card; a bird card can pay for a non-bird dominance card. Taking it does not activate it.

answer.part: Whether taking or activating consumes a Marquise action
answer.ruling: Taking and activating dominance are separate and neither requires a faction action allowance.
With two players remove all four dominance cards; shuffle the shared deck and each player draws three cards.

Cover four R slots with ruins. Map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea and 2 coins. If Vagabond is present during its setup, hide one each of R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword, one under each ruin; shuffle stacks and return them to empty R slots with identities hidden. Without Vagabond, ruins have no hidden items.
answer.evidence: Setup, step 4 and Hidden ruin items

answer.ruling: Set up factions in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond.

answer.part: Keep placement and movement permissions; Field Hospitals; rebuilding
answer.ruling: Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing, but other players may move pieces into it. Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply; this can happen outside battle. Without a Keep there is no hospital destination. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed.

answer.part: Marquise Daylight order and action allowance
answer.ruling: Craft first with workshops, then take up to three actions plus one action per bird card spent outside an action, in any order and number subject to Recruit's limit.

answer.part: March, Recruit limit and Overwork cost
answer.ruling: March is up to two moves and is one compound action that cannot be interrupted. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and is limited to once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.

Choose a clearing you rule with an open slot and a building type. Take the leftmost building of that type. Pay the column's full cost by removing wood from the target clearing or other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP on the uncovered track space. You need the full wood cost, building, and legal slot.

answer.part: Eyrie Birdsong steps and recovery placement
answer.ruling: In order: if hand is empty, draw one (Emergency Orders); add one or two hand cards to Decree with at most one bird, each to any column; then, only if no roosts are on map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.

Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card in column order Recruit, Move, Battle, Build; choose freely among cards within a column. Recruit card suit matches a roost clearing and places one warrior at one chosen roost there (Charismatic places two); Move suit matches origin and requires moving at least one warrior under normal move rules; Battle suit matches the battle clearing and initiates a battle with Eyrie warriors and an enemy; Build suit matches target and places a roost in a clearing you rule with an open slot and no roost already there. Bird cards are wild. Any required action that cannot be fully completed causes immediate Turmoil; cannot skip it or continue to another column.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties > Daylight — resolve the Decree; Decree table

answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties > Daylight — resolve the Decree

answer.ruling: Lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement, flipping all leaders face up first if none are face up; retuck Viziers into the new leader's columns. End Daylight and proceed to normal Evening: score roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, discard to five. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings.

When another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) per affected move, not per warrior. If they lack a matching card including birds, they show their hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters.
If Supporters is full, discard the incoming Outrage card; the payment or no-match draw still occurs. Merely battling in the clearing is not a trigger unless sympathy is removed.

answer.part: Alliance Revolt and Spread Sympathy procedures
answer.ruling: Both occur in Birdsong, and all Revolts must be completed before any Spread Sympathy; each may be done any number of times. Every supporter spent matches target clearing (birds wild). Revolt: choose a sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base still on board; spend two matching supporters; remove all enemy pieces and score one VP per enemy building/token removed; place matching base, warriors equal to sympathetic clearings matching the base's printed suit (including this one), and one warrior in Officers. Spread Sympathy: choose an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if none is on map; spend matching supporters shown above next sympathy space, plus one matching supporter if the target has at least three warriors of one other player (Martial Law); place token and score uncovered VP. Only one sympathy per clearing; Keep placement ban applies. Once spreading begins no return to Revolt that Birdsong.

Train by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. Each officer allows one Evening operation and operations do not consume officers. Organize removes one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, places sympathy there and scores its uncovered VP; no supporters, adjacency, or Martial Law payment, but token placement must be legal.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance > Daylight and Evening operations

answer.ruling: Discard all supporters matching that base's clearing, including birds, and remove half the officers rounded up. If no bases remain, discard excess supporters down to five. Apply whenever a base is removed.

answer.part: Vagabond Refresh, Slip, Move, forest Rest and Evening draw
answer.ruling: Birdsong Refresh: count tea already face up on Refresh track; flip two exhausted items face up per tea, then three more; tea refreshed now gives no bonus refresh and damaged status does not change. Optional Slip moves to adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors; ignores effects preventing movement out. Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if destination has any Hostile faction warriors; ignores rule, cannot enter forest, and from forest can move only to adjacent clearing. In forest during Evening, Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel face up and moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if able; it does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Always draw one card plus one per face-up coins on track, even after Rest.
Exhaust torch in a ruin's clearing; take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track and score one VP if item taken. Remove ruin when its last item is taken, freeing slot.

In matching clearing, choose face-up quest and exhaust its two listed items; put it completed in play area and choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards. Draw a replacement quest. No card cost.
Exhaust hammer; move one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face. Ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space.

Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except the special allied-battle-loss timing. On your own turn in battle, Infamy adds one VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first caused Hostility; no Infamy on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a Hostile marker out of Hostile, though it can still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another piece of its faction. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
answer.evidence: Vagabond > Relationships > Hostile; Daylight > Strike; Aid

answer.part: Coalition eligibility, activation and partner selection
answer.ruling: Vagabond cannot activate normal dominance. With four or more players, during own Daylight at 10+ VP, activate dominance to coalition with a player not already in a coalition, whose VP is lowest among players other than Vagabond; choose among ties. Place score marker on partner's board and stop scoring.
If partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including by dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies; coalition does not grant Allied powers. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent.
Card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play. Follow general and faction rules together when possible; if incompatible, faction rule wins. Cannot is absolute unless explicitly overridden.

answer.part: Unclear simultaneous resolutions and interruption of March
answer.ruling: If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses; for battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. Marquise March's two moves form one compound action and cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action.
At-start effects precede all other phase effects; at-end effects follow everything else in that phase, before the next phase.
Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.
Hand size is public but contents private; reveal/show a hand only when explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched/inspected; deck cannot.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases > Cards and hand information

answer.ruling: Agreements are non-binding; cards may be transferred only as instructed by rules, and actions require no consent.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases > Cards and hand information

answer.ruling: When the shared deck empties, immediately shuffle the discard pile into a new deck.

answer.part: Bird substitution for discards and bird costs
answer.ruling: Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple same-suit payments. If instructed to give or discard cards of a non-bird suit, treat birds as that suit; a non-bird cannot substitute when the instruction explicitly requires a bird.

answer.part: Shortage, proxies, fewer placements, cost and Decree
answer.ruling: Pieces are finite and proxies are not allowed. If unable to place all prompted pieces, place the maximum possible; cannot voluntarily place fewer. Shortage does not waive costs or prerequisites, nor Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions (an incomplete required action causes Turmoil).
answer.evidence: Actions > pieces finite and maximum possible; Eyrie > Decree

answers.evidence: Actions > Shared movement, crafting and battle; Eyrie Dynasties

answer.part: Normal origins and destinations, removed items and simultaneous effects
answer.ruling: Pieces placed normally come from supply or leftmost track space; removed faction pieces return to supply or rightmost empty track space. Items removed from game are permanently removed. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.
answer.evidence: Actions > Removed faction pieces; Special Rules > Place/remove/replace

answers.evidence: Actions > Shared movement, crafting and battle; Special Rules & Edge Cases

answer.ruling: Resolve forced actions as if the affected player chose them, retaining that player's abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its own battle decisions.

answer.part: Enemy replacement in Keep clearing and swap distinction
answer.ruling: Replace requires both removal and placement to be possible; the Keep placement ban cannot be bypassed by replacing an enemy piece. Swap ignores move/place restrictions.
The tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins, including the current player.

answer.part: Forest adjacency and Winter river for Slip
answer.ruling: A forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by one printed path. On Winter, the river also divides forests as paths do.
answer.evidence: Actions > Shared movement, forest definition; Vagabond > Slip

answer.ruling: Fall has no special rules.

answers.evidence: Actions > forest definition; Setup; Vagabond > Slip

answer.ruling: Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Place Keep in any corner starting clearing. Put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among the Keep clearing and its adjacent clearings, in any combination respecting slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks right to left, leaving the leftmost space empty.

Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader, keep others face up nearby, tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into that leader's listed columns. Fill roost track with the other six roosts from right to left.

Supply 10 warriors; put three bases in matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track; draw three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from the three-card hand. Start with no map pieces or officers.

Choose Thief, Tinker or Ranger and place pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Place each other faction's relationship marker at Indifferent. Take character's S-marked starting items: tea, coins and bags face up on matching tracks, other items face up in Satchel; return unused S items to box.

answer.part: Recommended Reach totals and faction values
answer.ruling: Recommended total Reach: at least 17 for two players, 18 for three, 21 for four. Base reach: Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. Law allows any mix totaling at least 17 for adventurous groups.

answer.part: Wood production, limits and Evening draw
answer.ruling: Birdsong places one wood per sawmill in its clearing (one per sawmill even if multiple share a clearing). Overwork in Daylight spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there. Both draw from finite supply of eight wood. Evening draws one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discards hand to five.
answer.evidence: Marquise > Wood production, Birdsong and Evening

answer.ruling: Recruit one warrior at each recruiter, only once per turn. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place the maximum available and choose among eligible recruiters where to place them.

answer.part: Eyrie item craft scoring and Builder
answer.ruling: Eyrie crafted items score one VP instead of printed VP due to Disdain for Trade; other extra crafting-point effects still apply. Builder ignores Disdain for Trade.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties > Lords of the Forest and Disdain for Trade; Leader table

answer.part: Leader Vizier columns and special abilities
answer.ruling: Builder: Recruit, Move; ignores Disdain for Trade. Charismatic: Recruit, Battle; each Recruit places two warriors. Commander: Move, Battle; one extra hit as attacker. Despot: Move, Build; when removing at least one enemy building/token in battle, gains one extra VP beyond normal removal points.

answer.part: Charismatic Recruit with only one warrior available
answer.ruling: No. Each Charismatic Recruit must place two warriors; if it cannot be completed fully, immediately enter Turmoil. General maximum-placement rule does not waive the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Decree Recruit; Turmoil; maximum possible rule

answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties; Actions > Shared movement, crafting and battle

answer.part: Guerrilla War dice and warrior caps
answer.ruling: When Alliance defends, Alliance uses higher die and attacker lower. Warrior caps still apply.

answer.part: Supporters use, inspection and hand limit
answer.ruling: Supporters can be inspected by Alliance and spent only for suit. They do not count as hand cards or toward hand limit; Alliance crafting is from hand, so Supporters cannot be used to craft.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance > Guerrilla War/Supporters; Daylight > Craft

answer.part: Spread then Revolt in same Birdsong
answer.ruling: No. Complete all Revolts before starting Spread Sympathy; once spreading starts, cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong, so new sympathy cannot support same-Birdsong Revolt.

answer.part: Martial Law with two players at two warriors each
answer.ruling: No. Martial Law adds a supporter only if the target has at least three warriors of one other player; two enemy players with two each do not qualify.
No Martial Law cost applies to Organize; it spends no supporters and has no adjacency requirement, but legal token placement is still required.

answer.part: Placing warriors or moving only pawn into sympathy
answer.ruling: Placing warriors in a sympathetic clearing does not trigger Outrage; moving only Vagabond pawn there does not trigger it. Outrage is triggered by moving warriors into sympathy or removing sympathy.
Moving allied warriors into sympathy triggers Outrage, because warriors move into the sympathetic clearing.
answer.evidence: Vagabond > Allied benefits; Woodland Alliance > Outrage

answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance > Outrage; Vagabond > Allied benefits

answer.part: Alliance Evening operations and officer use
answer.ruling: Operations are Move, Battle, Recruit and Organize; take up to your number of officers, in any order and repetition. Officers stay on board and are not consumed. Recruit places one warrior at one clearing with a base.
After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard hand to five.
The pawn cannot be removed. An enemy effect removing all enemy pieces from its clearing instead damages three items.

answer.part: Vagabond rolled hits and defenseless status
answer.ruling: Maximum rolled hits, attacking or defending, equals all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or down. Exhausted but undamaged swords count; damaged swords do not. Vagabond is defenseless only with no undamaged swords.
Each hit damages one undamaged item of Vagabond's choice; ignore excess hits when none remain.

answers.evidence: Vagabond > Daylight > Battle; Pawn and items

answer.ruling: Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately move to empty matching track space if possible; each track holds at most three of its type. Exhausting an item on track sends it to Satchel. Damaging moves an item to Damaged box without changing face. Ready tea/coins/bags may move to tracks when repaired or rested if space.
answer.evidence: Vagabond > Pawn and items; Repair; Rest

answer.ruling: Damaged items cannot pay actions.

At Evening capacity is six plus two per face-up bag on its track. Count Satchel plus Damaged box; track items do not count. Permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within capacity. Do not check immediately when acquiring an item.

answer.part: Forest Rest versus Refresh and Repair
answer.ruling: Forest Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; it does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Refresh flips exhausted items face up based on tea on Refresh track plus three more, without changing damage. Repair exhausts hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face.
answer.evidence: Vagabond > Birdsong Refresh; Daylight Repair; Evening Rest

answer.ruling: Exhaust one face-up undamaged item of any type and give a card matching your clearing to a player with faction pieces there, even if Hostile. You may then take one item from their Crafted Items into Satchel/track; no available item is required to Aid.

To advance a non-Hostile marker one space, Aid that faction as many times in the same turn as printed between current and next spaces. One Aid counts toward only one improvement; advance and score VP printed in new space. At Allied, each subsequent Aid scores two VP.

answer.part: Allied Aid points and movement/attack benefits
answer.ruling: At Allied, each subsequent Aid scores two VP. Vagabond may force warriors of one Allied faction to accompany pawn movement, subject to their normal move restrictions; cannot accompany a move specified to be alone. As attacker at battle start, may treat warriors of one Allied faction in clearing as own, adding them to undamaged swords for maximum rolled hits. They may fight a different enemy; cannot attack their own faction.

answer.part: When allied warrior losses cause Hostility
answer.ruling: In battle using allied warriors as your own, may absorb hits by removing those warriors or damaging items. If more allied warriors are removed than items damaged in that battle, ally becomes Hostile at battle end. Equal numbers do not trigger it. This special rule overrides normal hostility timing for these friendly warriors taken as hits against another enemy.
answer.evidence: Vagabond > Taking hits with an ally

answers.evidence: Vagabond > Taking hits with an ally

answer.ruling: No, a single clearing cannot pay fox and rabbit icons because current clearing must match every icon. The Vagabond pawn may be reused repeatedly in a turn, but each icon still requires a face-up undamaged hammer.
answer.evidence: Actions > Craft > Vagabond cost and reuse; Vagabond > Craft

answer.ruling: When Vagabond crafts an item, it may immediately take it face up into Satchel/track and use it for another Daylight action if cost and other requirements are met.

Thief starts boot, torch, tea, sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from a player with faction pieces in your clearing. Tinker starts boot, torch, bag, hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take discard-pile card matching clearing (bird always qualifies). Ranger starts boot, torch, crossbow, sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items keeping their faces and immediately ends Daylight, beginning Evening.
Explore removes a ruin when its last hidden item is taken, freeing the building slot. Ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed; ordinary building placement does not remove them.
answer.evidence: Vagabond > Explore; Actions > Shared rules on ruins

answer.part: Coalition partner as enemy and Allied powers
answer.ruling: Coalition partners are not enemies and coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

Two warriors yield 0 ordinary removal VP each. Removing one building yields 1 ordinary VP. Since battle is on Vagabond's own turn and the faction became Hostile when the first warrior was removed, that triggering warrior gets no Infamy; the second hostile warrior gives 1 Infamy VP and the hostile building gives 1 Infamy VP. Total: 1 building removal + 2 eligible Infamy = 3 VP.
answer.evidence: Scoring > Ordinary removal VP; Vagabond > Hostile/Infamy

answer.ruling: Into hostile buildings/tokens only, cost is one boot because Hostility requires an extra boot only for hostile warriors. Into hostile warriors from several factions, cost is two boots total: one normal plus one extra if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction.

answer.part: Taking dominance card and activation/action cost
answer.ruling: Taking an available card puts it in hand; activation is a separate act and does not occur immediately. During Daylight, taking and activating neither requires a faction action allowance.

Faction-piece ownership cannot change: each player owns the faction chosen at setup and its listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces and possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.
Resolve an immediate-effect crafting card, then discard the card to shared discard. Keep a persistent-effect card in your play area.
A persistent card in play is outside your hand and cannot be spent, discarded or used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.

answer.part: Crafting and permitted uses of Ambush/Dominance
answer.ruling: Neither Ambush nor Dominance cards can be crafted. Defender may play matching Ambush for two immediate hits; attacker may play matching Ambush to foil a defending ambush. Dominance may be activated to change victory condition or spent for suit.

answer.part: Starting player, seating, score and dice
answer.ruling: Choose starting player and seating randomly; put score markers at zero and battle dice nearby.
Faction setup order is Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond and is distinct from turn order. Turns proceed clockwise.
First to 30 VP wins immediately, on any player's turn; no need to finish action, phase or turn.
Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. Battle does not require ruling the clearing.

answers.evidence: Actions > Shared movement, crafting and battle

answer.ruling: If both sides have applicable before-roll effects or after-roll effects at the same timing, attacker chooses the order. The side taking hits chooses the order of effects triggered by removal of its pieces.
answer.evidence: Actions > Battle, before-roll/after-roll and Deal hits

answer.ruling: In Count Hits, add extra hits and subtract hits ignored.

answer.part: Non-Vagabond item crafting source, destination and VP
answer.ruling: The item token comes from map item supply and goes to crafting faction's Crafted Items box. Score VP printed on card, subject to Eyrie's Disdain exception.

answer.part: Eyrie and Alliance crafting pieces, suit and wildcard icon
answer.ruling: Eyrie activates roosts and Alliance activates sympathy; each icon requires one matching clearing suit. A piece's suit comes from its clearing, not card suit. Three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit.
Add one hand card to Supporters. With no base, keep at most five and discard overflow; with any base, no cap.
Craft, Mobilize and Train may be taken in any order and number; Alliance need not finish crafting first.

answer.part: Eyrie Evening score and draw, including after Turmoil
answer.ruling: Score VP on rightmost empty roost-track space, draw one card plus uncovered draw bonuses, then discard to five. This full normal Evening still occurs after Turmoil.
Exhaust one sword to initiate Battle. An exhausted undamaged sword counts toward rolled-hit maximum but is face down and cannot pay an action; payment requires a face-up undamaged item.
answer.evidence: Vagabond > Daylight > Battle; Pawn and items

answer.part: Turn phase order and next turn
answer.ruling: Each turn is Birdsong, Daylight, Evening; turns proceed clockwise, so after Evening the next player clockwise takes their turn.

Each hit damages one undamaged item of Vagabond's choice, moving it to Damaged box without changing its face. Already-damaged items cannot absorb another hit; excess hits are ignored when no undamaged items remain.
Take up to your number of officers in operations, in any order/repetition; officers are not consumed. One Recruit operation places one warrior at one clearing with a base.

answer.part: Vagabond Daylight action count and ordering
answer.ruling: Take actions in any order and number as ready undamaged items permit; no fixed sequence and action types may be repeated, subject to each action's item costs and requirements.
Exhaust one crossbow to Strike. Actions require a face-up undamaged item, so an exhausted or damaged crossbow cannot pay.
answer.evidence: Vagabond > Daylight > Strike; Pawn and items
